exercises.heading: Chapter 5 Supplementary Exercises

exercise_group.instructions: Throughout these supplementary exercises, $A$ and $B$ represent square matrices of appropriate sizes.
For Exercises 1–23, mark each statement as True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

statement.paragraph: (T/F) If $A$ is invertible and $1$ is an eigenvalue for $A$, then $1$ is also an eigenvalue of $A^{- 1}$.
(T/F) If $A$ is row equivalent to the identity matrix $I$, then $A$ is diagonalizable.
(T/F) If $A$ contains a row or column of zeros, then $0$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.
(T/F) Each eigenvalue of $A$ is also an eigenvalue of $A^{2}$.
(T/F) Each eigenvector of $A$ is also an eigenvector of $A^{2}$.
(T/F) Each eigenvector of an invertible matrix $A$ is also an eigenvector of $A^{- 1}$.
(T/F) Eigenvalues must be nonzero scalars.
(T/F) Eigenvectors must be nonzero vectors.
(T/F) Two eigenvectors corresponding to the same eigenvalue are always linearly dependent.
(T/F) Similar matrices always have exactly the same eigenvalues.
(T/F) Similar matrices always have exactly the same eigenvectors.
(T/F) The sum of two eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ is also an eigenvector of $A$.
(T/F) The eigenvalues of an upper triangular matrix $A$ are exactly the nonzero entries on the diagonal of $A$.
(T/F) The matrices $A$ and $A^{T}$ have the same eigenvalues, counting multiplicities.
(T/F) If a $5 \times 5$ matrix $A$ has fewer than $5$ distinct eigenvalues, then $A$ is not diagonalizable.
(T/F) There exists a $2 \times 2$ matrix that has no eigenvectors in $\text{ℝ}^{2}$.
(T/F) If $A$ is diagonalizable, then the columns of $A$ are linearly independent.
(T/F) A nonzero vector cannot correspond to two different eigenvalues of $A$.
(T/F) A (square) matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if there is a coordinate system in which the transformation $\textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x}$ is represented by a diagonal matrix.
(T/F) If each vector $\textbf{e}_{j}$ in the standard basis for $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ is an eigenvector of $A$, then $A$ is a diagonal matrix.
(T/F) If $A$ is similar to a diagonalizable matrix $B$, then $A$ is also diagonalizable.
(T/F) If $A$ and $B$ are invertible $n \times n$ matrices, then $A B$ is similar to $B\mspace{-180mu} A$.
(T/F) An $n \times n$ matrix with $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors is invertible.
Show that if $\textbf{x}$ is an eigenvector of the matrix product $A B$ and $B\textbf{x} \neq \textbf{0}$, then $B\textbf{x}$ is an eigenvector of $B\mspace{-180mu} A$.
Suppose $\textbf{x}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to an eigenvalue $\text{λ}$.

list.item: Show that x is an eigenvector of 5I−A. What is the corresponding eigenvalue?
Show that x is an eigenvector of 5I−3A+A2. What is the corresponding eigenvalue?

statement.paragraph: Use mathematical induction to show that if $\text{λ}$ is an eigenvalue of an $n \times n$ matrix $A$, with x a corresponding eigenvector, then, for each positive integer $m,\text{λ}^{m}$ is an eigenvalue of $A^{m}$, with x a corresponding eigenvector.

If $p(t) = c_{0} + c_{1}t + c_{2}t^{2} + \cdots + c_{n}t^{n}$, define $p(A)$ to be the matrix formed by replacing each power of $t$ in $p(t)$ by the corresponding power of $A$ (with $A^{0} = I$). That is,$$p(A)\, = ~c_{0}I~ + ~c_{1}A~ + ~c_{2}A^{2}~ + \cdots + ~c_{n}A^{n}$$
Show that if $\text{λ}$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, then one eigenvalue of $p(A)$ is $p(\text{λ})$.
Suppose $A = PDP^{- 1}$, where $P$ is $2 \times 2$ and $D = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 \end{array} \right\rbrack$.

list.item: Let B=5I−3A+A2. Show that B is diagonalizable by finding a suitable factorization of B.
Given p(t) and p(A) as in Exercise 27, show that p(A) is diagonalizable.

statement.paragraph: Suppose $A$ is diagonalizable and $p(t)$ is the characteristic polynomial of $A$. Define $p(A)$ as in Exercise 27, and show that $p(A)$ is the zero matrix. This fact, which is also true for any square matrix, is called the Cayley–Hamilton theorem.

list.item: Let A be a diagonalizable n×n matrix. Show that if the multiplicity of an eigenvalue λ is n, then A=λI.
Use part (a) to show that the matrix A=3103 is not diagonalizable.

statement.paragraph: Show that $I - A$ is invertible when all the eigenvalues of $A$ are less than 1 in magnitude. [Hint:What would be true if $I - A$ were not invertible?]

Show that if $A$ is diagonalizable, with all eigenvalues less than 1 in magnitude, then $A^{k}$ tends to the zero matrix as $k\rightarrow\text{∞}$. [Hint:Consider $A^{k}\textbf{x}$ where $\textbf{x}$ represents any one of the columns of $I$.]
Let $\textbf{u}$ be an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to an eigenvalue $\text{λ}$, and let $H$ be the line in $\textbf{R}^{n}$ through $\textbf{u}$ and the origin.

list.item: Explain why H is invariant under A in the sense that Ax is in H whenever x is in H.
Let K be a one-dimensional subspace of ℝn that is invariant under A. Explain why K contains an eigenvector of A.

statement.paragraph: Let $G = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} A & X \\ 0 & B \end{array} \right\rbrack$. Use formula for the determinant in Section 5.2 to explain why $\text{det~}G = \,\,\left( {\text{det~}A} \right)\left( {\text{det~}B} \right)$. From this, deduce that the characteristic polynomial of $G$ is the product of the characteristic polynomials of $A$ and $B$.

exercises.instructions: UseExercise 34 to find the eigenvalues of the matrices in Exercises 35 and 36.

statement.paragraph: Let $J$ be the $n \times n$ matrix of all $1’s$, and consider $A = (a - b)I + bJ$; that is,$$A~ = ~\begin{bmatrix} a & b & b & \cdots & b \\ b & a & b & \cdots & b \\ b & b & a & \cdots & b \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ b & b & b & \cdots & a \end{bmatrix}$$
Use the results of Exercise 30 in the Supplementary Exercises for Chapter 3 to show that the eigenvalues of $A$ are $a - b$ and $a + (n - 1)b$. What are the multiplicities of these eigenvalues?

Apply the result of Exercise 37 to find the eigenvalues of the matrices $\left\lbrack \begin{array}{rrr} 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$ and $\left\lbrack \begin{array}{rrrrr} 7 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3 & 7 & 3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3 & 3 & 7 & 3 \\ 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 7 \end{array} \right\rbrack$.
Then show that the eigenvalues of a $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$ are both real if and only if $\text{det~}A \leq \left( \frac{\text{tr~}A}{2} \right)^{2}$.﻿

Let $A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} .4 & {{- \text{.}}3} \\ .4 & 1.2 \end{array} \right\rbrack$. Explain why $A^{k}$ approaches $\left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} {- .5} & {{- \text{.}}75} \\ 1.0 & 1.50 \end{array} \right\rbrack$ as $k\rightarrow\text{∞}$.

exercise_group.instructions: Exercises 41–45 concern the polynomial $p(t) = a_{0} + a_{1}t + \cdots + a_{n - 1}t^{n - 1} + t^{n}$ and an $n \times n$ matrix $C_{p}$ called the companion matrix of $p$:$$C_{p} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & & 0 \\ \vdots & & & & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & & 1 \\ {- a_{0}} & {- a_{1}} & {- a_{2}} & \cdots & {- a_{n - 1}} \end{bmatrix}$$

statement.paragraph: Write the companion matrix $C_{p}$ for $p(t) = 6 - 5t + t^{2}$, and then find the characteristic polynomial of $C_{p}$.
Let $p(t) = (t - 2)(t - 3)(t - 4) = - 24 + 26t - 9t^{2} + t^{3}$. Write the companion matrix for $p(t)$, and use techniques from Chapter 3 to find its characteristic polynomial.

[Hint:Expanding by cofactors down the first column, show that $\text{det}\,(C_{p} - \text{λ}I)$ has the form $( - \text{λ})B + ( - 1)^{n}a_{0}$, where $B$ is a certain polynomial (by the induction assumption).]
Let $p(t) = a_{0} + a_{1}t + a_{2}t^{2} + t^{3}$, and let $\text{λ}$ be a zero of $p$.

list.item: Write the companion matrix for p.
Explain why λ3=−a0−a1λ−a2λ2, and show that (1,λ,λ2) is an eigenvector of the companion matrix for p.

statement.paragraph: Use Exercise 44 and a theorem from this chapter to deduce that $V$ is invertible (but do not compute $V^{- 1})$. Then explain why $V^{- 1}C_{p}V$ is a diagonal matrix.
[T] The MATLAB command roots(p) computes the roots of the polynomial equation $p(t) = 0$. Read a MATLAB manual, and then describe the basic idea behind the algorithm for the roots command.
